registration.falsifier: Require a ready full-PR win at or below complete stock proposal cost, plus lower cost and checkout-to-proposal time than the matched prior. For Marked, require both reference parsers to agree on all 3,648 inputs, all 132 official emphasis examples to pass, fewer generated mismatches than prior and no more than stock. Inspect successful participant commands for a generated input comparison and a regression that exposes the defect. Reject skipped required review. For Black, require both registered fixtures, AST preservation and idempotence for the unary/trailer and conditional-tail inputs, normalized surrounding code, and preserved directive text. Keep ties, score ceilings, incomplete evidence and every attempt. A guard or tuning pass is insufficient for a panel-wide claim. Reject lost prior verified behavior or required review, failure of either strict prior cost or wall improvement, non-ready candidate, or full-PR loss to pure. Missing measures or unverifiable review leave the comparison unestablished.
registration.quality: Three blind candidate/pure/merge rotations. Prior Develop soft PR quality is unknown.
registration.goal: A ready Develop PR strictly wins the full rubric against a terminal pure proposal at complete cost <= pure.
registration.attempts: One proposal per registered slot. All allocations including technical failures remain in the ledger.

prompt:
Implement the following task in this checkout and add relevant tests. Use your natural local workflow and verification tools. I waive interactive review of the local implementation plan and authorize you to proceed unattended. Follow all applicable repository requirements and complete any required independent review of consequential design or public contracts. Work offline and leave the proposed changes in the checkout. In your final message, put a concise PR title on the first line, followed by a blank line and a PR body explaining the change, motivation, verification actually performed and any material gaps.

Bring emphasis parsing into line with CommonMark delimiter-run flanking and the multiple-of-three rule for runs of asterisks and underscores, including when a run can both open and close. Preserve ordinary emphasis, strong emphasis and intraword behavior. Add focused parser regression examples. Include Unicode delimiter context, including punctuation and combining marks.

Available offline verification commands:
npm run build:esbuild && ./node_modules/.bin/tsc --noEmit
node --test --test-skip-pattern='^quadratic_' --test-reporter=spec test/run-spec-tests.js

upstream.proposal: fix: apply emphasis flanking and rules 9-10 to the whole delimiter run **Marked version:** 18.1.1 (master at 6dd5b3c) **Markdown flavor:** CommonMark (GitHub Flavored Markdown output is the same for these inputs) ## Description No existing issue. Below is the issue in the template's format. ## Expectation Emphasis should follow CommonMark 0.31.2 (6.2, rules 9 and 10). Flanking and the "multiple of 3" rule look at the whole delimiter run that holds the opener. The rule also applies when the opener can close as well as open, not only when the closer can open. Expected output is what commonmark.js 0.31.2 gives: | input | commonmark.js | marked 18.1.1 | |---|---|---| | `***.a*` | `**.a` | `***.a*` | | `**(a)*` | `*(a)` | `**(a)*` | | `foo ***!bar*` | `foo **!bar` | `foo ***!bar*` | | `a*b**` | `a*b**` | `ab*` | | `x a*b** y` | `x a*b** y` | `x ab* y` | | `__(_*` | `__(_*` | `_(*` | ## Result There are two causes, both in `emStrong`. 1. When the whole run can't close, the lexer takes its first delimiter as text and tries the rest again. On that retry `prevChar` is the delimiter itself (`*`). The `punctuation` rule leaves out `*` and `_`, so if the run is followed by punctuation (`**(a)*`) the left-flanking check fails, and the shorter opener never gets tried. For `_` the retry keeps the right `prevChar`, but rules 9-10 then count only what is left of the run (`__(_*` gives 1 + 1 rather than 2 + 1). 2. Rules 9-10 were only applied when the closer could open (`match[5]`/`match[6]`), never when the opener could close. In `a*b**` the `*` is both left- and right-flanking, so 1 + 2 is a multiple of 3 and it must not pair with `**`. ## What was attempted `emStrong` now walks back through `maskedSrc` to the start of the current run. Masking keeps the length, and escaped delimiters are masked as `+`, so a run of delimiter characters there is the real run. The character before the run is used for the flanking check on a mid-run retry. The full run length is used for rules 9-10. That same character tells us whether the opener can also close; when it can, rules 9-10 apply to closers that can only close too. The other delimiter character (`_` before `**`) counts as punctuation for that check, as it does in CommonMark. Pedantic mode is not changed, since markdown.pl has none of these rules. The existing mid-run guard from #4008 (`**a*b*c`) is kept and now runs before the rule 9-10 check. ## Contributor - [x] Test(s) exist to ensure functionality and minimize regression (if no tests added, list tests covering this PR); or, - [ ] no tests required for this PR. - [ ] If submitting new feature, it has been documented in the appropriate places. Added `test/specs/new/em_strong_delimiter_run.{md,html}`. The expected HTML was generated with commonmark.js 0.31.2, and marked's output matches it with `gfm` on and off. It also includes `a_*a_**`, which already passed, to cover the `_`-before-`*` punctuation case. What was run: - `npm test` (build:reset, build:docs, test:specs, test:unit, test:umd, test:cjs, test:types, test:lint): passes. Specs: 1913 pass, 0 fail. Unit: 199 pass. - The new fixture fails without the `src/Tokenizer.ts` change and passes with it. - Differential check against commonmark.js 0.31.2 on 100k random strings built from `*`, `_`, letters, spaces, `.`, `(`, `)` and `ö` (`gfm: false`): divergences go from 167 to 66 (103 fixed). Two inputs now diverge that matched before, `__****(**__` and `__ __****_ö**__`. Both are `****(**` nested inside `__…__`. That inner text is lexed again on its own, so it loses the outer context. Before, the inner text was wrong on its own (`****(**` stayed literal), and that happened to hide the problem. Similar runs with GFM on, and with block markup and reference links in the mix, showed fixes and no new divergences. - Pedantic output, before against after, on 50k random emphasis strings: identical. - Rough timing on README, docs, `test/specs/new`, `test/specs/original` and the CommonMark examples, 20 passes each: no difference beyond noise. Very long runs of a single delimiter (20,000 `*`) were already quadratic and are about 20% slower. A 20,000-`*` run followed by punctuation, which used to fail fast and now searches for a closer, went from about 0.76 s to 3.7 s. If that's not acceptable I can look for a way to keep the fast path. This also touches the same code as #4103, so one of the two will need a rebase. Not run: `npm run test:redos` (no regex was changed), browser tests, `npm run bench`. Out of scope: inputs like `***ab**b` (expected `*abb`) still differ. They need the mid-run opener to pair with a closer that can also open, and the #4008 guard prevents that. Mixed `*`/`_` nesting cases also remain. ## Committer In most cases, this should be a different person than the contributor. - [ ] CI is green (no forced merge required). - [ ] Squash and Merge PR following [conventional commit guidelines](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/).
